title: Risk 0.5% vs 2% per trade: 1,000 runs
takeaway: With the same trades, risking 2% of the account per trade instead of 0.5% grew faster but made the typical worst drop about four times deeper (−23% vs −6%), because losing streaks hit everyone. Choose the size whose worst drop you could sit through.
learn: Risk per trade is how much of your account you lose when a stop hits.
With the same trades, risking 2% instead of 0.5% made the typical worst drop about four times deeper: −23% vs −6%.
Losing streaks happen to everyone: the typical run had 9 losses in a row, which costs about 17% at 2% a trade.
Pick a risk per trade whose worst drop you could sit through, before the streak arrives.
question: Same edge: what changes if you risk 2% instead of 0.5%?
emotion: the stomach drop of a −23% hole you didn't see coming, then the calm of choosing your size on purpose

captions: The only difference: how much each trade risked.

captions: We simulated 1,000 traders. Same edge, two sizes.
Risk per trade means what you lose when a stop hits.
In this run, 2% grew more: +117% vs +23%.
It also fell almost four times deeper.
All 1,000 runs at 0.5%. Typical worst drop: −6%.
At 2%, the typical worst drop was −23%.
Almost 1 in 5 runs fell over 30% at some point.
